raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From the Dakota, make your way to the American Museum of Natural History, about a 12-minute walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"You've just passed the Dakota, where John Lennon was shot dead in the street outside on December 8, 1980, and where Yoko Ono still lives.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Across from it lies the tear-shaped garden Yoko partly funded, with its grove of elms and the Imagine mosaic.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Here's a place that changes its mind in public: a few years ago, scientists here concluded that dinosaurs never dragged their tails through the mud but waved them in the air as they walked.","source_id":"9fc88552-1383-4dab-8f25-646cfa9d9e35","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"So the curators took apart the famous skeletons, bone by bone, and rebuilt them with tails erect, then set one skeleton over a slab of Texas riverbed where fossilized footprints show no tail-drag marks at all — a peephole into how a scientific theory takes hold.","source_id":"9fc88552-1383-4dab-8f25-646cfa9d9e35","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Since 1869 this has been the country's leading private scientific research center and its top museum for paleontology, zoology, anthropology, and now astronomy, and that constant traffic between researchers and curators is exactly what keeps it so fiercely alive.","source_id":"9fc88552-1383-4dab-8f25-646cfa9d9e35","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Come in through the newest door.","source_id":"02deacf1-1988-46dc-bad9-c72f4cbfe0da","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"In 2023 the $431-million Richard Gilder Center for Science, Education and Innovation opened, and its lobby stops you cold — 230,000 square feet of curving walls that mimic Southwestern canyons, a sinuous look made by spraying structural concrete straight onto rebar.","source_id":"02deacf1-1988-46dc-bad9-c72f4cbfe0da","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Behind those walls sits 12% of the museum's whole collection, an insectarium, a permanent butterfly vivarium, open storage exhibits, and a 360-degree Invisible Worlds Theater about the hidden networks that underlie all life.","source_id":"02deacf1-1988-46dc-bad9-c72f4cbfe0da","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"On the first floor, the Hall of Biodiversity pulls you toward \"The Spectrum of Life,\" a psychedelic wall of specimens.","source_id":"516484ad-1eb6-4a4b-82b5-26864938ede0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Nearby, an interactive rain-forest diorama layers video, sound, and even smell to drop you inside a rain forest, all of it pressing one point: how much we stand to lose if the variety and interdependence of Earth's life-forms unravels.","source_id":"516484ad-1eb6-4a4b-82b5-26864938ede0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Follow the crowds and you'll hit the first floor's favorite, the Milstein Hall of Ocean Life, where a beloved 94-foot blue whale hangs from the ceiling over dioramas on ecology and conservation and models of more than 750 sea creatures, from microscopic algae to glowing jellyfish.","source_id":"1c8b7c5f-fbde-4a19-9725-843f01563c86","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3,"also_cites":["6d387f81-b703-4bae-8938-1477b1e8b871"]},{"text":"Elsewhere you'll find animal halls, galleries devoted to gems, and an IMAX theater.","source_id":"6d387f81-b703-4bae-8938-1477b1e8b871","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"And at one entrance, a 63-foot, 19th-century canoe carved by the Haida people of British Columbia greets you.","source_id":"6d387f81-b703-4bae-8938-1477b1e8b871","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Up on the third floor, the Margaret Mead Hall of Pacific Peoples carries the life's work of the famous anthropologist who lived from 1901 to 1978 and spent most of that life in this museum's Anthropology Department.","source_id":"1d9507f9-78cf-48ed-9a97-c587b99306f9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Her hall roams the many cultures of the South Pacific islands, Polynesia and Micronesia among them, and its showpiece is a group of traditional masks carved from wood and bark in Papua New Guinea.","source_id":"1d9507f9-78cf-48ed-9a97-c587b99306f9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"On the museum's north side, don't miss the ultramodern Rose Center for Earth and Space, a giant glass cube wrapped around the Hayden Planetarium.","source_id":"98765bad-9dfd-4b10-8077-ac63f81e5b64","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Inside, a powerful reality simulator flies you through space to witness the Big Bang, and past the Hall of Planet Earth the Cosmic Pathway winds you through 13 billion years of evolution.","source_id":"98765bad-9dfd-4b10-8077-ac63f81e5b64","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Walking with kids? The Discovery Room lets them pretend to dig up dinosaur bones, work through a scavenger hunt, and peer down microscopes — but it runs on timed free tickets, so grab one early in the day before they're gone.","source_id":"8a7f3731-01d6-42db-acf8-40fd721fcf70","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"First time here? Consider a guided introductory tour; they start at a quarter past each hour until 4:15pm, led by volunteer guides who train for six months, and no two hit quite the same highlights.","source_id":"24e3930b-7737-45d1-878b-729f25524d7e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"One last tip: this place is a magnet for school groups, so it's crowded by midmorning, and attendance runs opposite the weather — sparse on a lovely day, and when it's blustery or rainy, watch out.","source_id":"33fccc1c-4a01-46df-b2bd-e8c65556a9f2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3}]}
